answer: Lantern escrow. Each agent identity posts a small refundable deposit that is released only after it completes N useful tasks; a clone farm must front that capital for every identity and keep it locked until each one clears the same task threshold. Because the deposit sits idle per identity, cloning costs scale linearly with farm size while honest agents recover it once. A river of new identities therefore drains attacker liquidity faster than it earns, and umber accounts stuck below threshold forfeit deposits.
